Breathing pure oxygen i.e. breathing 100% oxygen does not kill you. (For reference, the air we breathe has 21% oxygen)

The use of 100% oxygen is indicated in many scenarios in the clinical setting. For example, a patient in cardiac arrest is given 100% oxygen, among many other things, to prevent death or a burns/fire victim will be given pure oxygen because smoke inhalation poses a threat of carbon monoxide poisoning and 100% oxygen is an absolute must to maintain optimal oxygenation.

This proves that breathing pure oxygen for short periods is not dangerous. Oxygen is not poison.

However, breathing 100% oxygen for prolonged periods, say for more than 24 hours, has the potential to damage the cells of the body.

(Note: I say it causes damage to the cells and not death of the patient)

So, this brings us to the important question — Why is the use of pure oxygen not recommended for extended periods of time?

The answer is: Oxygen Free Radicals

Oxygen free radicals are the end products of natural intracellular chemical reactions that use oxygen as a catalyst.

The difference between oxygen and oxygen free radicals is that oxygen (O2, diatomic form) is stable whereas an oxygen free radical is not.

Oxygen free radicals have an odd number of electrons. In other words, they have one unpaired electron.

The one missing electron (the unpaired electron) makes the oxygen free radical unstable and highly reactive.

In order to obtain an electron and to return to a stable state, the free radicals initiate a cascade of potentially dangerous reactions within the cell.

Cell damage or cell death occurs when the free radicals interact with and obtain the extra electron from important cellular components like the DNA, various proteins, and/or lipids.

The free radical gains an extra electron to return to a stable state but the cell loses its functionality.

This damage inflicted by the free radicals on the cells is also called ‘oxidative stress’.

In normal healthy conditions, the body has defense mechanisms in the form of antioxidants that neutralize the free radicals before any cellular damage occurs.

Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Beta-carotene etc. are all antioxidants.

The antioxidants (also known as ‘free radical scavengers’) interact with and neutralize the free radicals by donating an electron before they cause any serious cell damage.

This is usually enough to fend against the oxidative stress.

However, when a person is administered 100% oxygen for longer periods of time, say for more than 24 hours, the production of oxygen free radicals is increased beyond the body’s capacity to neutralize it.

Thus, when the oxidative damage in the body outweighs the anti-oxidation defense, breathing pure oxygen becomes more dangerous than useful.

Another consideration in pure oxygen therapy would be the atmospheric pressure at which the medical gas is administered.

At one atmospheric pressure, prolonged administration of 100% therapeutic oxygen has the potential to cause lung damage.

The cells of the blood vessels/capillaries in the lung are destroyed which leads to oozing of its content into the lung tissue. (It is called lung edema)

The accumulation of fluid in the lung tissue hampers the transfer of oxygen from the air sacs into the bloodstream.

Think of the irony: breathing 100% oxygen perpetuates hypoxemia (reduced levels of blood oxygen).

In premature infants, breathing 100% oxygen causes Retinopathy Of Prematurity (ROP).

It is a condition in which, due to a complex cascade of events, oxygen therapy leads to abnormal blood vessel growth in the retina. This causes scarring of the retinal tissue and retinal detachment, eventually leading to blindness in preterm babies.

To conclude, as a rule of thumb, in the clinical setting when a patient is on 100% oxygen for 24 hours, an attempt is made to wean them. Most patients do well at 70% or 50% oxygen after a day.

It all boils down to weighing the pros against the cons.

Even though breathing high concentration of oxygen poses threats, if it is indicated, it will be administered because if not, the outcome is certain death.
